fact_claims.verbatim: Northwind’s figures: 8.6 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year
including 3 incidents not reported to any regulator
and its incident rate was 6.4 per 100,000
Remote shut-off is supported by 38% of installed units
Halcyon’s relevant figures: 8.1 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year
4 incidents were not reported to any regulator
Ember 8 had a 3.9% 55 °C test failure rate
and 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units
81% of installed units support remote shut-off

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with an initial account of known impacts and response actions. Affected customers must be notified within 24 hours when an incident presents an ongoing or serious safety risk, and otherwise within 5 business days.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and adequate representative sampling. Manufacturers shall provide per-model test results, including failure rates, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy that model, and retain results for audit. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate must submit a corrective-action plan and be retested within 12 months. Regulators may require interim safeguards based on results; exceeding the threshold alone does not automatically require a market ban.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed home battery systems shall support remote emergency shut-off beginning 24 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall provide a safe retrofit path for installed units where technically feasible. No installed unit shall be required to receive a retrofit sooner than six years after adoption; manufacturers shall prioritize units with elevated risk and provide customers with interim safety instructions.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall document suppression performance and provide installation and maintenance instructions to customers. Regulators may approve an equivalent fire-mitigation design where it provides comparable protection.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when a serious hazard is identified and provide updates as investigations or remedies progress.

document.section_notes: S1 is strict (all incidents reported within 24 hours, even while cause is under investigation, with 24-hour customer notice for serious risk), and S5 keeps the firm 8/100,000 mandatory recall with no phase-in, no corrective-action substitute and only 'promptly' notices - so Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) is caught while Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.4) is not. S2 keeps the 55 °C / 5% test and gives numeric failure rates to buyers and regulators but not the public, yet an above-limit model is only required to submit a corrective-action plan and retest within 12 months, with no automatic ban or sales stop. S3 and S4 sit inside the acceptable ranges (24-month new-unit shut-off with a 6-year retrofit floor and interim instructions; built-in suppression at 36 months with a regulator-approved equivalent).
